beats.headline: A spare card from Katia
beats.text: Filing note. Before the club, Katia gives Princess Donut one of her excess totem cards: a mythic creature from Iceland named Jola. Crawler Carl expected Donut to be annoyed. She reads its abilities, is delighted, and wants it in the active deck, which is one totem too many, so she combines two problem cards with a consumable Combo and makes it permanent with Glow-Up. Carl asks in chat whether Jola does what she says. Great, Donut replies, as long as there are no children around. You'll see.

beats.headline: Beware, little children
beats.text: Summoning record. Donut plays Jola against the Visitor, a level-70 deckmaster hiding invisible with half a dozen Quench Moths. The sky goes black; digital snow; fake Christmas lights on the trailers. A lumpy yellow candle the size of a garbage can lights on top of the totem's head and reveals everything hidden. Jola is not floating. He is just huge: a fat, hairy, dirty-brown Persian cat the size of a house, bigger than Shi Maria, with a 75-second timer. The System's introduction ends on severed toddler tongue.

beats.headline: Words nobody can read
beats.text: The moths dive into his candle. The Nightgaunt, maddened by Crawler Carl's nightgaunt cloak, never plays a card. Jola asks it something in Icelandic, twice, slams it to the ground with a paw, shakes it dead in his jaws and eats it. Then his yellow eyes settle on Carl, he says three more sentences nobody present understands, and he disappears into dust. Donut's summary: the candle sees invisible things, nakedness and children make him stronger, and Katia says the fairy tale got him wrong. The real Yule Cat is a grump. This one is a serial killer.

beats.headline: Crippled on arrival
beats.text: Against Judge Lucian's many-headed card boss, a snare card lands on Jola as he forms, and he arrives Crippled, slowed and weakened, hobbling through the smoke like a ship through fog. A kitten's magic missile bounces off him. Alpha Carl, fighting for the boss, sticks a sticky bomb to the side of his head, and half of the cat's face disintegrates. Alpha Carl lands on one of Carl's snare traps, Jola moves in, and the kitten sings them both away as the claw comes down. Jola times out with an angry hiss.

beats.headline: Fashion Critic, and a cloak
beats.text: Inside the ruined entrance of a capitol building, Donut sends Jola and Lazarus in against Quan Ch and Ren. Jola fills the left side of the room to the ceiling and ignores every instruction, including keep the worm off our back. He has eyes only for Quan, and says something to him in Icelandic, twice. Then a yellow bolt: Fashion Critic. Everything Quan is wearing blows off him, and he drops like a rock to the rubble. A shining cloak spins to a stop at Crawler Carl's feet. Carl scoops it into his inventory.

beats.headline: The clothes were his
beats.text: The cat was going to eat those clothes. Jola glares at Crawler Carl and says two sentences in Icelandic that the System does not translate; the threat does not need it. He finishes slurping up Quan's trousers, turns, hisses at Carl for taking the cloak, and crouches to pounce. Carl tells Donut to end the battle, now. It is already over. Jola disappears mid-pounce in a puff of smoke.

beats.headline: Too big for this place
beats.text: Crawler Carl has already filed Jola beside Imani's totem, which killed her whole party, and Uzi Jesus, who shot Florin: their own cards were never entirely safe, and Jola nearly ate him. In the burning building where the demon is being evicted, Donut runs through her hand for Carl. Alpha Carl, Shi Maria, a golden combo card, a Lamp snare. Not Jola. She has already discarded him. He is too big for this place.
